scope: P2 chapter-upload policy availability, exact accepted-source recovery, and upload regression
production_behavior: Terms, privacy and guidelines must each contain validated inline text or an HTTP(S) policy URL; optional operator branding/contact are separate.
Missing policy content rejects new upload begin/edit, page intake/replacement, resumable draft changes, immediate commits and new schedules.
Ordinary authenticated safe reads/cancellation remain available under existing ownership and authority checks.

Exact committed receipt replay remains available. Accepted source recovery requires exact immutable command/payload, current authority and a healthy verified actual source receipt; no source signing, staging or republishing is called.
Unknown commands and immutable original pins are retained; missing policies do not authorize replay or purge.

includes: licensed 24-PNG originals, 2 chapters, 4 notices, attributed cover

publication_access_http.coverage: Actual accepted source followed by local transaction rollback; lost wrapper acknowledgement simulated by prepared state; missing-policy altered payload refused; exact receipt materialized; rebuilt router/config repeated request without duplicate source events.

verified.fixture_cleanup: Every reported runtime test completed through run-auth-tests.sh with exit 0; guard requires unforced verified process cleanup and closed ports.

test_development_notes: The new cross-transport policy test initially used an unsupported Z timestamp suffix; corrected to existing canonical schedule_time helper.

Its native requests initially omitted the required x-weebdex-expected-account header; corrected to the existing native transport contract. Both initial failures were fixture errors, not relaxed assertions or product bypasses.

The 25 preexisting public_uploads scenarios ran from an executable snapshot built from the same final production source before the final test-only header/timestamp corrections. The added scenario ran from the rebuilt final test executable.
limits: These are automated HTTP/router/database tests, not browser acceptance or production deployment proof.
The policy-loss receipt case recreates the router/config, not a full OS process restart. Separate existing scheduled/publication tests cover runtime restart behavior.
Licensed fixture cache/image bytes must not be included in public source or recovery uploads.
